To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the correlation between two halves of a test is not a reliable measure of the correlation between two hypothetical forms of the test, because (b) the two halves are not independent, and (c) the correlation between the actual and the hypothetical forms depends on the relative size of the variances.

the use of a single form to estimate reliability can be justified if the test is short enough, if the test is administered under standardized conditions, if the test has a high reliability, and if the test is not used to make important decisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of changes in the variables involved in the estimation of test reliability.
the effect of the changes of the variables involved in the computation of the reliability coefficient upon the value of the coefficient.
the development of a method for determining the reliability of a single form test, based upon an estimate of the reliability obtained from the split-half method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reliability coefficient is not a constant but a variable, and that the magnitude of its variability is dependent upon the nature and the magnitude of the variables involved in its estimation.

, in general, the reliability coefficient is a function of (1) the reliability of the available form, (2) the correlation between the scores of the available form and those of a hypothetical form, (3) the correlation between two hypothetical forms, and (4) the ratio between the number of items in the available and hypothetical forms.
the reliability of a split-half test is a function of the reliability of the total test, the number of halves, the standard deviations of these halves and the intercorrelation of the halves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reliability coefficients of the test are affected by changes in the variables involved.

, in the case of the Spearman-Brow n formula, the reliability coefficient of a test computed through the split-half method may be estimated from the reliability coefficient of the test computed through the correlation of equivalent forms.
we have developed a set of formulas that can be used to estimate the reliability of a single test from its actual data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use machine learning techniques to predict the reliability of a measurement system based on the data collected from it.
there is no single best method for calculating the reliability coefficient, and that the method you use should be determined by the characteristics of your data.
, while it is possible to use a variety of methods to estimate test-retest reliability, the results of these methods can be quite different.
